statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-66822 (GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7) is a .NET information disclosure issue in System.Net.Http: SocketsHttpHandler can keep a Proxy-Authorization header across an HTTP redirect and leak basic proxy credentials to the destination server. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected platforms and the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/448, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships System.Net.Http.dll at its own .NET version, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in that version's runtime pack, NativeAOT runtime pack and runtime archives held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap. The other copies of System.Net.Http.dll are reference assemblies with no implementation code, and the net461 and net471 System.Net.Http support assemblies in the SDK build extensions, which are used only by applications built for .NET Framework on Windows. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on, on both architectures. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-66822 (GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7) is a .NET information disclosure issue in System.Net.Http: SocketsHttpHandler can keep a Proxy-Authorization header across an HTTP redirect and send basic proxy credentials to the redirect target. Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/448, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135697, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The .NET 10 fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 06ffb53d14eaf3e703cd2ef2f19e92509081463d on release/10.0.1xx ('[HTTP] Clear proxy auth header on redirect'), which makes RedirectHandler clear the Proxy-Authorization header together with the Authorization header and changes no other file outside tests; it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/06ffb53d14eaf3e703cd2ef2f19e92509081463d. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source and published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives each dotnet-sdk-10 build holds (seven in 10.0.301-0 to 10.0.302-1, eight from 10.0.400-1 on). The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one implementation copy of System.Net.Http.dll, a managed .NET assembly in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>. It also carries a reference assembly of the same name under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/<version>, which holds only API metadata and no implementation code, and three System.Net.Http.dll assemblies for .NET Framework in the SDK directory (under Microsoft/Microsoft.NET.Build.Extensions/net461 and net471, and TestHostNetFramework), which contain no SocketsHttpHandler or RedirectHandler code. No other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The shared-framework copy is byte-identical, on each architecture, to System.Net.Http.dll in Microsoft's Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64 or linux-arm64 package of the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. Every one of these copies records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. In Microsoft's 10.0.13, 10.0.14 and 10.0.15 builds of the assembly, the redirect code sets both the Authorization and the Proxy-Authorization header to null; in the 10.0.9 to 10.0.12 builds it clears only Authorization (we read this from the IL of Microsoft's linux-x64 and linux-arm64 builds of each version, which are byte-identical to the copies above). The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-66822 (GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7) is a .NET information disclosure issue in System.Net.Http: SocketsHttpHandler can keep a Proxy-Authorization header when it follows an HTTP redirect and send basic proxy credentials to the destination server. Microsoft lists the .NET 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 and fixed in 9.0.21: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/448, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. The .NET 9 fix is dotnet/runtime commit acba91f7ce3541c606dbfcd974f9b7aea0f9816d ('[HTTP] Clear proxy auth header on redirect'), which makes the redirect handler in RedirectHandler.cs clear the ProxyAuthorization header next to the Authorization header; it is in the v9.0.21 tag and not in v9.0.20: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/acba91f7ce3541c606dbfcd974f9b7aea0f9816d. DHI dotnet-sdk-9 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET 9 SDK for Linux (feature band 9.0.3xx), which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We inspected every package built from this source that the DHI Debian repository publishes as of 2026-11-28, versions 9.0.315-0, 9.0.316-0, 9.0.316-1, 9.0.317-1, 9.0.318-0, 9.0.318-1, 9.0.319-0, 9.0.320-0, 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, for amd64 and arm64: the dotnet-sdk-9 packages, and the dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages, which hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog; no debug-symbol packages are published. Each package was checked against its index checksum and its whole payload was read, including every file inside the five nupkg archives each dotnet-sdk-9 build carries (an FSharp.Core library pack and four project and item template packs). The shared framework and SDK versions are 9.0.17 and 9.0.315 in 9.0.315-0, 9.0.18 and 9.0.316 in 9.0.316-0 and 9.0.316-1, 9.0.19 and 9.0.317 in 9.0.317-1, 9.0.20 and 9.0.318 in 9.0.318-0 and 9.0.318-1, 9.0.21 and 9.0.319 in 9.0.319-0, 9.0.22 and 9.0.320 in 9.0.320-0, and 9.0.23 and 9.0.321 in 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, the same on both architectures. Every dotnet-sdk-9 build carries one implementation copy of the .NET System.Net.Http.dll, in the shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>; two reference assemblies with no implementation code, under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/<version> and /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/NETStandard.Library.Ref/2.1.0; and three .NET Framework builds of System.Net.Http.dll used by the SDK's .NET Framework build extensions (net461 and net471) and its .NET Framework test host, byte-identical in every build, which contain neither SocketsHttpHandler nor RedirectHandler (the same search finds both names in the shared framework copy). No other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The shared framework copy records the dotnet/runtime tag commit it was built from: v9.0.17 to v9.0.20 in the builds up to 9.0.318-1, and v9.0.21, v9.0.22 and v9.0.23 from 9.0.319-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. Its IL agrees: the instruction sequence that sets both the Authorization and the ProxyAuthorization header to null is absent from every copy up to 9.0.318-1 and present once in every copy from 9.0.319-0 on, on both architectures. The range ends at 9.0.319-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-66822 (GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7) is a .NET information disclosure issue in System.Net.Http: SocketsHttpHandler can keep a Proxy-Authorization header when it follows an HTTP redirect and send basic proxy credentials to the destination server. Microsoft lists the .NET 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 and fixed in 9.0.21: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wxxw-5cvc-53j7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/448, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. The .NET 9 fix is dotnet/runtime commit acba91f7ce3541c606dbfcd974f9b7aea0f9816d ('[HTTP] Clear proxy auth header on redirect'), which makes the redirect handler in RedirectHandler.cs clear the ProxyAuthorization header next to the Authorization header; it is in the v9.0.21 tag and not in v9.0.20: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/acba91f7ce3541c606dbfcd974f9b7aea0f9816d. DHI dotnet-sdk-9 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET 9 SDK for Linux (feature band 9.0.3xx), which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We inspected every package built from this source that the DHI Debian repository publishes as of 2026-11-28, versions 9.0.315-0, 9.0.316-0, 9.0.316-1, 9.0.317-1, 9.0.318-0, 9.0.318-1, 9.0.319-0, 9.0.320-0, 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, for amd64 and arm64: the dotnet-sdk-9 packages, and the dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages, which hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog; no debug-symbol packages are published. Each package was checked against its index checksum and its whole payload was read, including every file inside the five nupkg archives each dotnet-sdk-9 build carries (an FSharp.Core library pack and four project and item template packs). The shared framework and SDK versions are 9.0.17 and 9.0.315 in 9.0.315-0, 9.0.18 and 9.0.316 in 9.0.316-0 and 9.0.316-1, 9.0.19 and 9.0.317 in 9.0.317-1, 9.0.20 and 9.0.318 in 9.0.318-0 and 9.0.318-1, 9.0.21 and 9.0.319 in 9.0.319-0, 9.0.22 and 9.0.320 in 9.0.320-0, and 9.0.23 and 9.0.321 in 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, the same on both architectures. Every dotnet-sdk-9 build carries one implementation copy of the .NET System.Net.Http.dll, in the shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>; two reference assemblies with no implementation code, under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/<version> and /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/NETStandard.Library.Ref/2.1.0; and three .NET Framework builds of System.Net.Http.dll used by the SDK's .NET Framework build extensions (net461 and net471) and its .NET Framework test host, byte-identical in every build, which contain neither SocketsHttpHandler nor RedirectHandler (the same search finds both names in the shared framework copy). No other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The shared framework copy records the dotnet/runtime tag commit it was built from: v9.0.17 to v9.0.20 in the builds up to 9.0.318-1, and v9.0.21, v9.0.22 and v9.0.23 from 9.0.319-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. Its IL agrees: the instruction sequence that sets both the Authorization and the ProxyAuthorization header to null is absent from every copy up to 9.0.318-1 and present once in every copy from 9.0.319-0 on, on both architectures. The range ends at 9.0.319-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
